reason: The cited evidence does not address Mg-containing HEAs in a metastable solid-solution state, their decomposition into Mg-rich intermetallics, or the link to corrosion/oxidation resistance. E1 discusses Mn depletion in CrMnFeCoNi, and E2 mentions as-cast structures with precipitates but no Mg-specific transformation or property correlation, leaving all key premises unsupported.
premises: Mg-containing lightweight HEAs can be prepared in a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution state
During thermal aging, this solid solution decomposes via diffusion-controlled nucleation and growth of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds
This phase segregation causes local elemental depletion/enrichment in the matrix
The altered local chemistry changes the formation and stability of protective oxide scales and passivation layers
The microstructural evolution correlates with either retained or diminished corrosion and oxidation resistance
